| [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md) | Where every constraint capacity turns over at a positive rate and is produced only by others, with no basal production and production vanishing as its producers do, capacities whose production graph is acyclic all decay to zero: a capacity that persists needs a productive cycle among its ancestors, and removing a feedback edge set extinguishes every capacity; a cycle is necessary and not sufficient, and a one-member cycle is not closure | From A10 §1 and §5A of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), after the owner's "try to progress the theoretical program". What it adds to the record is the boundary with closure: the necessary cycle may be a self-loop, and a self-loop is not closure in [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)'s sense or [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s, which need two or more constraints. | Active |
| [CLAIM-529](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, a different individuation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). Their abstract says transitions in individuality are hard to describe without circularity, since the features used are products of the transition, and claims a non-circular description that the body never argues. The body holds the parts of an answer, and they are of two kinds. Criteria on interactions (per-member accounting of benefit, entrenchment order, knockout of interaction types, release from a scaffold) can test a declared candidate without assuming it is a unit ([CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md)), and the scaffold test needs the declared boundary ([CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)). Criteria on members' attitudes toward the group (shared goal, belonging, focal goal of sustaining it) individuate constitutively, which is not the non-circular route and is unavailable for organisms without such attitudes. It does not say the paper argues this, and it leaves the presupposed lower-level units where the paper leaves them. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-531](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure. Entrenchment as they define it is a one-way dependency order, and a tree rooted in its core passes their knockout test; closure needs the core to depend in turn on the set. By [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md), read for interactions, an acyclic order persists only on outside supply, which is their own scaffolded conexus. It does not say their communities lack closure, only that entrenchment and knockout do not show it; and it reads Wimsatt's concept only as they quote it. | Proposed |
